source.title: Analysis of classifiers robust to noisy labels

record.file_problem: The supplied text appears to be the full paper, including appendix and references; no garbling or cutoff noted.
record.tranche_reason: The paper trains classifiers on datasets with class-conditional random label noise and reports test accuracy, including comparisons with uncorrected baselines. These results refine the claim’s smooth-degradation version but do not test fitting a completely random labeling to zero training error.
record.gate_note: The paper reports test accuracies on noisy-label datasets and comparisons of noise-correction methods with baselines. It does not report training error, zero training error on random labels, chance test error, unstructured inputs, explicit regularization, or a real-versus-random learning order. Reported test-accuracy results are rows for V4 insofar as they measure performance across stated noisy-label settings; no training-fit evidence is reported.
record.test_reason: The paper takes networks' tendency to overfit noisy labels as background motivation and evaluates noise-correction methods. It reports no training-fit measurements, random-versus-real learning dynamics, or controlled degradation trajectory toward fully random labels. Its mitigation results do not test the listed versions.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors also conclude that their transition-matrix estimator is accurate, based on comparison with supplied FashionMNIST matrices. They report Importance Re-weighting as best on CIFAR, improvements from all three methods on FashionMNIST0.6, and suggest that FashionMNIST0.5's supplied matrix may be inaccurate. These are the authors' interpretations; improved classification accuracy does not directly establish more accurate transition estimates.
record.recipe_differences: Uses class-conditional label-noise datasets and compares noise-correction classifiers by clean test top-1 accuracy; it does not use the original random-label memorization experiment or report training error.
record.method_sensitivity: Results differ by dataset and correction method: FashionMNIST0.5 shows little difference from baseline for Forward and Importance Re-weighting, while FashionMNIST0.6 and Cifar10 show different patterns.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 6.5.4 reports approximate clean-test accuracies for baseline, Forward, Importance Re-weighting, and T-Revision: CIFAR 0.54, 0.51, 0.60, 0.565; FashionMNIST0.5 0.91, 0.91, 0.905, 0.93; FashionMNIST0.6 0.82, 0.86, 0.86, 0.865.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Noise-correction methods can improve clean-test accuracy under class-conditional label noise, with benefits depending on the dataset and method.

fits_no_version.finding: Table 2 reports transition-matrix estimation errors of approximately 0.158 and 0.09 for the two FashionMNIST datasets.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Anchor-based estimation can approximate supplied class-conditional noise transition matrices in these experiments.

record.code_released: not stated (the appendix says a repository is linked but supplies no URL)
record.problems: No training error is reported; test accuracies in the results discussion are approximate, while mean and standard deviation are described but not given numerically in the text. Several accuracy trajectories are presented only as figures. The exact label-corruption proportions and construction for the named datasets are not fully explained in the supplied text.
record.rows_left_out: No rows retained: the text’s numeric and approximate test-accuracy comparisons are outcomes of noise-correction methods on noisy datasets, but do not establish the training-set fitting behavior named in V4. Figure 8–10 trajectories are figure-only and do not specify the needed fit or corruption sweep; Figures 11–13 compare methods by test accuracy.

untested.parts: Fitting completely random labels to near-zero training error, chance test performance, and unchanged architecture and hyperparameters.
Relative fitting time and convergence speed across corruption fractions.
Training-set fitting on shuffled, independently permuted, or Gaussian-noise inputs.

Perfect training fit as corruption increases and a controlled test-error trajectory from clean labels to fully random labels. Two noisy FashionMNIST settings and correction-method comparisons do not establish this trajectory.
Effects of weight decay, dropout, and augmentation on random-label fitting and true-label generalization.
Whether shared real-data patterns are learned before noisy labels.

record.verdict_notes: Replace the record's tests/T5 classification and V4 tested status. The empty result-row set is appropriate for these claim versions. The supplied transition matrices describe three classes with diagonal probabilities 0.5 and 0.4, so the noise settings retain label signal and are not completely random labeling. Differences between the two baseline test accuracies alone do not demonstrate V4's training-fit and degradation pattern.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not report fitting a completely random labeling, training error, chance test error, or unchanged architecture and hyperparameters for such a test.
No training-time comparison for fitting random versus true labels or corrupted-label fractions is reported.
No shuffled-pixel, permuted-pixel, or Gaussian-noise input experiments are reported.

Test accuracies are reported for datasets named FashionMNIST0.5, FashionMNIST0.6, and Cifar10, but the text does not state that these represent a sweep from no corruption through fully random labels, nor does it report training-set fit or a steadily rising error trajectory. Figure-only accuracy trajectories lack textual values.
The paper does not test weight decay, dropout, data augmentation, or their removal.
No learning-order comparison between real and noisy or random labels is reported.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

relation.reason: The introduction takes deep networks' tendency to overfit noisy labels as background motivation without measuring that behavior.

tranche.reason: The study evaluates noise-correction methods using clean test accuracy and transition-matrix estimation. It reports no results testing any claim version.

source_check.notes: The pack lists no rows, synthesis statements or verdicts. Clean test accuracy under class-conditional noise does not establish training-set memorization or the degradation trajectory specified by V4.
